correctness.rationale: For a>b all global graph automorphisms preserve the unequal degree classes. Every induced partial isomorphism has exactly one of the side-preserving and side-exchanging forms, with uniquely recovered occupied sides. Extendible maps are pairs of within-part partial injections, counted by R_aR_b. Nonextendible maps split into exactly two single-direction nonempty cross-part injections and a two-direction union, counted by 2C+C². Positive coefficients of C in ranks 1..b imply the exact support 1..2b and top coefficient (binom(a,b)b!)². Direct exhaustive partial-injection enumeration matches all rank coefficients for eight parameter pairs including balanced controls, but is not used as a proof of infinite scope.

originality.rationale: The 2015 graph inverse-semigroup treatment builds induced-subgraph inverse monoids but gives ideal/idempotent structure rather than rank-refined extension obstruction counts. The published finite homogeneous rank theorem covers K_{a,a} but its equal-size hypothesis excludes K_{a,b}, a>b; its formula does not imply the asymmetric nonextension census. The multipartite square-zero census concerns the strict f^2=0 subfamily, and therefore does not yield a count of all partial automorphisms or extendibility. published-finding corpus searches for aliases, exact formula and extension thresholds found no stronger covering statement. value.rationale: Graph partial-automorphism extension is a canonical symmetry property, not a parameter picked merely for an easy count. The result exactly partitions the entire inverse monoid of every asymmetric biclique into extendible and nonextendible maps by domain rank; the factorization gives all finite rank coefficients and the sharp 2b threshold past which every local symmetry is global. The top obstruction coefficient quantifies maximum failures; the abrupt contrast with equal-side homogeneous graphs has natural structural motivation and may guide higher-part and nonhomogeneous extensions.
